issues_confirmed: nn/model.py:124 — train_test_split splits ROWS, but the table's grain is the line item (69,956 rows over 49,793 orders / 645 variants) and all 11 KEY_TARGETS are order-, customer- or variant-level attributes. Counted from data/line_items.csv: items per order are 35,060x1, 10,224x2, 3,588x3, 921x4, so 34,896 rows (49.88%) sit in a multi-item order. Simulating the same 80/20 split (seed 0): 6,054/13,991 = 43.27% of val rows have a sibling line item from the same order in train.

nn/data_builder.py:426-431 + :451 — I rebuilt the exact order+customer-grain feature vector a has_refund run sees after the LEAKAGE_MAP drops (five money columns, utm_source/medium/campaign, discount_code, month/dow/hour, the six customers.csv columns, city, postcode_district, four email aggregates): 49,791 of 49,793 orders have a GLOBALLY UNIQUE fingerprint. The order primary key is fully reconstructable from surviving features, so the sibling-row overlap is a literal lookup, not a weak correlation.

nn/model.py:124 — measured the lookup directly on has_refund: 5,974/13,991 val rows (42.7%) have an exact train fingerprint match, that match maps to ONE label in 5,974/5,974 cases, and the label is correct 5,974/5,974 = 100%. A pure fingerprint-lookup rule with no model scores accuracy 0.9466, precision 1.0000, recall 0.6171 (TP 1,204 / FP 0 / FN 747 / TN 12,040) against a naive all-zero baseline of 0.8606. 61.71% of val positives are directly readable off train. Published AUC is 0.8436 (REPORT.md:174).

nn/evaluate.py:360 — variant_return_rate is a per-variant constant on a line-item table. 645 variants, median 85 rows each, min 2, so 13,991/13,991 = 100% of val rows have their variant in train; (variant_price, weight_grams, inventory_quantity, option1_value, option2_value) identifies 645/645 variants uniquely. A per-variant train-mean lookup gives RMSE 0.000000 and R^2 1.000000 vs naive-mean RMSE 0.042528. Any number published for this KEY_TARGET would be a memorisation score.

nn/evaluate.py:359 — delivery_delay_days is identically 0 on all 69,956 rows. data/purchase_orders.csv has 21 POs and actual_delivery == expected_delivery on all 21 (delay distribution {0: 21}, zero nulls); po_line_items has 645 rows / 645 distinct variants, all resolving to a PO, so every variant gets 0.

nn/data_builder.py:555 — get_X_y types delivery_delay_days as BINARY, not the 'regression' REPORT.md:517 claims, because set(unique).issubset({0,1,True,False}) is satisfied by the one-element set {0.0}. So `python nn/evaluate.py --all` builds the table, trains eight full models, then dies at nn/model.py:219 with 'Only one class present in y_true' before reaching variant_return_rate or city. Corroborated inside the repo: REPORT.md:505-519's summary table has figures for KEY_TARGETS 1-8 and '—' for exactly rows 9, 10 and 11. The command is documented at REPORT.md:158, :495, README_nn.md:45, :127 and HOW_TO_USE.md:395-407 and has never run to completion.

nn/data_builder.py:555 — same single-value bug confirmed still present for quantity (all 69,956 line_items rows are 1; 1 distinct value) and n_escalations. n_escalations is identically 0 because the rule at :241-244 looks for a 'bot' message followed by a 'human' one, but data/support_messages.json senders are customer (3,108), bot (1,204) and agent (700) — no 'human' sender (stale name repeated at :231 and :252). Renaming to 'agent' does not help: transcripts have only two shapes, customer|bot|customer|agent|customer (700) and customer|bot|customer (504), so bot is never adjacent to agent. Recomputed the current rule end-to-end: 0 escalations across all 1,204 tickets.

nn/model.py:174 vs :212-226 — UNCHANGED since 2026-10-19. all_preds/all_targets are reassigned at the top of every epoch's validation block, so after model.load_state_dict(best_weights) they still hold the FINAL epoch's predictions. nn/evaluate.py:376-391 feeds the same stale arrays into every metric suite, while permutation_importance (nn/estimator.py:514) and --save_model (:527) use the restored weights.
nn/model.py:202-212 — UNCHANGED. If val_loss is NaN on epoch 1, 'inf - nan > min_delta' is False, so best_weights stays None and model.load_state_dict(None) raises a bare AttributeError.

nn/data_builder.py:68-69 — UNCHANGED. _load_refunds computes refund_variant_ids then discards it on the next line; the merge at :356 is on order_id, so refunds are labelled at order grain on a line-item table. 5,843 refunds over orders containing 10,025 line items -> 4,182 rows (41.7% of the positive class) mislabelled; the correct positive count is 5,850 (5,836 refunds match one line-item row, 7 match two).

REPORT.md:190 — 'Interpretation: Leakage-safe' still sits directly under the '⚠️ Not leakage-free' banner added at :164-172, and still names size_issue (Δ=0.794) and damaged_in_transit (Δ=0.278) as the top two features — the two columns the banner says were wrongly present.

nn/data_builder.py:516, :524 — LabelEncoder and StandardScaler are fit on the full table inside _encode_and_scale, which runs before the split at nn/model.py:124, so val rows inform the scaling and the category vocabulary. Same root cause as the split finding: everything that should respect the split happens before it.

nn/data_builder.py:143-144 — UNCHANGED stale comment claiming 'Multiple POs per variant — keep most recent'. data/po_line_items.csv has 645 rows and 645 distinct variant_ids, so the sort_values/drop_duplicates is a no-op.

verdict: The engineering is clean; the evaluation methodology is the defect, and this run found its root. Three reviews have now patched LEAKAGE_MAP by hand, but the split itself (nn/model.py:124) is row-level on a line-item table while all 11 targets are entity-level attributes — 49,791/49,793 orders are uniquely fingerprinted by surviving features, so a no-model lookup beats the published has_refund numbers, and variant_return_rate is a free R^2 of 1.0. That channel is immune to every column drop, which makes REPORT's three 'pending re-run' figures premature. Separately, `--all` has never actually finished: it dies on delivery_delay_days (identically 0) at target 9 of 11, and REPORT's own summary table shows '—' for exactly rows 9-11. Four of the five tasks proposed on 2026-10-19 were never touched. The right move is still to fix the split and the stale-metric bug, add the structural test, and withdraw the numbers — not to build Phase 11.
